newsitem.title: KENYA: Zairean rebels capture town of Beni -- sources.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels capture town of Beni -- sources.

text.p: Zairean rebels backed by Rwanda have captured the town of Beni and local residents reported looting and raping by Zaire's ragged army as it fled further north, missionary group sources said on Monday.
"Beni fell on Saturday. Rebels moved swiftly to capture Beni after taking the town of Butembo," one of the sources told Reuters, quoting missionaries evacuated from eastern Zaire.
Beni, so far the northernmost town to fall to the rebels, is close to where the Ugandan army has been attacking Ugandan rebels based on the Zairean side of the border.

Zaire has accused Uganda of attacking and occupying the town of Kasindi, 60 km (35 miles) southeast of Beni and 10 km (six miles) inside Zaire. Uganda says it shelled Kasindi to neutralise the Ugandan rebels but denies crossing the border.

The Zairean rebels, who call themselves the Alliance of Democratic Forces for Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), now control much of eastern Zaire, including the towns of Uvira, Kamanyola, Bukavu, Goma and Butembo.
The ADFL rebels have vowed to take their military campaign in Africa's second largest country to the capital Kinshasa.
Africa's latest conflict was ignited by Zaire's attempts to expel the Banyamulenge -- an ethnic Tutsi group which first came to Zaire from Rwanda nearly 200 years ago.
The fighting has displaced over one million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees as well as many local Zaireans.

The Ugandan government newspaper New Vision said on Saturday that Ugandan troops crossed into eastern Zaire on Thursday to attack Ugandan rebel bases. It said 23 rebels were killed when the army seized Kasindi and the surrounding Virunga hills.
The Zairean rebels, an alliance backed by Uganda and Rwanda, are fighting Zairean government troops and forces of Rwanda's former Hutu government which was driven into Zaire in 1994.
The Kinshasa government says the Zairean rebel leader, Laurent Kabila, is the puppet of a coalition of ethnic Tutsi forces from Rwanda and Burundi, supported by Uganda.

Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni has close ties with the Rwandan military strongman, Vice-President and Defence Minister Paul Kagame. Kagame's Tutsi rebels drove Hutu government forces out of Rwanda in 1994 after the slaughter of an estimated one million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
